title: Auserene vs Stoic: routine journal or a meditation from your day?
seoTitle: Auserene vs Stoic (2026): AI journal, meditation, streaks, price
description: Auserene vs Stoic compared from Stoic's own pages, November 2026: meditation, streaks, AI and its providers, memory, free plan, price, Android and privacy.
dek: Stoic gives you morning and evening routines, a library of meditations and breathing, and streaks. Auserene writes a meditation from your day, keeps no streaks, and shows you what it remembers.
titleOptions: Auserene vs Stoic: routine journal or a meditation from your day?
Stoic vs Auserene: meditation, streaks and AI memory compared
Auserene or Stoic? An honest comparison from one of them
Is the Stoic app worth it? How it compares with Auserene

faq.a: It depends on what you want. Stoic is stronger on structured morning and evening routines, a big library of breathing exercises and meditations, and platforms, since it runs on Mac, Android and the web. Auserene is stronger if you want a meditation written from your own day, an evening conversation instead of a form, a memory you can read and edit, and no streaks. Auserene is iPhone only.

Yes. Stoic's App Store listing describes guided and unguided meditation with background sounds and timed chimes, and its Premium page lists 20+ breathing exercises. They're a library, the same for everyone. Auserene writes a new guided meditation from each day's conversation.

Stoic has a free plan with daily prompts, quotes, affirmations, basic guided journals and a limited selection of breathing and meditation exercises. Premium and Premium + AI are paid. The App Store lists several Premium and AI prices without billing periods, plus a $299 lifetime option, as of November 2026.

faq.q: Does the Stoic app use AI, and which provider?
faq.a: Yes, in its Premium + AI tier, and some on-device features on iOS 26. Stoic's help center says AI entries go to OpenAI and may be kept for up to 30 days, not for training. Its privacy policy names OpenAI, Anthropic or Google Gemini as providers.

Yes. Stoic has streaks and badges, which its plans page lists under Premium. You can turn them off and restore a missed streak by completing past check-ins. Auserene has no streaks; its habit goals have a 21, 42 or 64-day finish line and never mark a missed day red.
Yes. Stoic has an Android app and a web app, but its help center says the Android app has fewer features than iOS and can't sync with the iOS app yet. Auserene is iPhone only.

informationGain: A disclosed head-to-head built only from Stoic's own pages on November 19, 2026, including its App Store prices that carry no billing periods, the mismatch between its help center (OpenAI, current entry only) and privacy policy (OpenAI, Anthropic or Google Gemini, historical journals) on AI, and its device-and-iCloud storage model, set against Auserene's meditation written from your day, readable memory and no streaks.
